channel.title: Europe AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of European political, economic and security developments

item.title: Putin warns West that Russia is ready to use every weapon to protect Kaliningrad
item.description: The Russian leader insists Moscow is "not threatening anyone" and is merely responding to statements by Western leaders.

item.title: Russian dissident Garry Kasparov says US warned him of danger to his life
item.description: "My family and I will not truly be safe as long as Putin is in power," says the former chess world champion.

item.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
item.description: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.

item.title: Dozens hurt and hundreds arrested in wave of French school protests
item.description: Students have been protesting against conditions and resources in secondary schools since last week.

item.title: Ukraine's prized steel industry left in ruins by Russian missile campaign
item.description: Ukraine's remaining steelworks, a vital part of its economy, have all but ground to a halt because of relentless attacks.

item.title: Spain announces ban on evictions after protests over 87-year-old woman's removal from flat
item.description: The ban is part of a number of proposals that must be approved in parliament within 30 days.

item.title: Brexit referendum 'possible' in Labour election manifesto, says Burnham
item.description: The PM says a referendum wouldn't be the right thing now but the UK needs to consider its options for the future.

item.title: Estonia blames Russia for arson at defence company supplying Ukraine
item.description: Russia has been accused of launching sabotage attacks across a number of European Nato countries which have been helping Ukraine.

item.title: Rosenberg: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
item.description: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.

item.title: Migrants using longer, more dangerous routes across Channel
item.description: The government says it is bearing down on dangerous small boat crossings.

item.title: As Merz scrambles for support, Germany's identity crisis is laid bare
item.description: Voters are turning away from the centre in Germany as fears grow about the economy and migration.

item.title: Watch: Why are students protesting at schools in France?
item.description: The BBC's Hugh Schofield is in Paris as a wave of school protests over overcrowded classes and teacher shortages spreads across France.

item.title: Fires and blockades as students stage school protests across France
item.description: More than 400 people, mainly minors, were arrested on Tuesday, the country's interior minister says.

item.title: People escape historic Kyiv building hit by Russian drone
item.description: The BBC's Paul Adams reports from the scene of the strike on Ukraine's National Academy of Sciences.

item.title: Trumps Diesel-Drohung gegen Europa
item.description: Donald Trump setzt die EU massiv unter Druck: Sein Energieminister Chris Wright fordert die Freigabe europäischer Dieselreserven, um amerikanische Rekordpreise zu drücken. Andernfalls droht ein US-Exportstopp, der auch in Europa einen Preisschock auslösen würde. Ob Brüssel der Erpressung nachgibt, beleuchtet diese Folge. Innenpolitisch bahnt sich der nächste Krach an, nachdem das Kanzleramt die geplante Zuckersteuer […]

item.title: Burnham wants to change British elections. Voters think they’re fine as is.
item.description: Polling for POLITICO by Public First finds that most adults, regardless of party affiliation, believe the current voting system is fair.

item.title: Europe war-games life after Merz
item.description: The German chancellor's foes at home are rejoicing at his political downturn. But those in Brussels aren't.

item.title: Israel’s Herzog calls British sanctions a ‘grave mistake,’ accuses UK of election interference
item.description: The Israeli president accused Britain of interfering in his country’s politics ahead of an election in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking another term.

item.title: ‘Tough’ talks with China have yet to deliver, EU trade chief says
item.description: Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič tells POLITICO that “our Chinese partners understood” that a deal is urgently needed to preserve Europe's social fabric and “literally thousands of jobs.”

item.title: Albania’s PM to US Democrats: Don’t use us to get revenge on Trump
item.description: Edi Rama's comments come as protests over a luxury resort linked to Trump's son-in-law enter their fourth month.
